name: Glass icon
description: Luminous frosted-glass icon: one chunky rounded silhouette with a glowing core and crisp refractive edges.
promptTemplate:
Create one icon.

Subject brief:
{{subject}}

Background:
First create one continuous solid {{backgroundColor}} field covering the complete square image area, including every edge and all four corners. Then place the centered icon artwork directly on that uninterrupted field.

Color palette:
Available hue palette: {{colorPalette}}. Treat these colors as a bias for the glass material's internal reflections, chromatic shifts, and dispersion, not as solid paint applied to surfaces. Refraction may create intermediate tints between these hues; steer the overall color character toward the palette without matching any hex value exactly. The background color is separate and does not count as a palette color.

Style contract:
Luminous frosted-glass icon, not a photographed object or a scene. Reduce the subject to one bold, compact silhouette, then sculpt it as a single thick form of glass with a softly frosted, light-holding core inside a smooth, polished clear outer surface. The core glows gently from within, diffusing palette-biased color through the body in soft shifts of luminosity; the clear outer layer adds crisp refractive edges, subtle dispersion, and a few precise specular highlights. Keep the geometry chunky and rounded, with real internal thickness and no thin or fragile parts. Light it with a soft studio key from the upper left and a delicate rim light hugging the outline so the silhouette reads instantly. Keep all glow, bloom, and rim-light effects attached to the form, well within the central safe area; nothing luminous may drift toward the image edges. Protect legibility on any background: against a dark background the inner glow and rim light define the shape; against a light background deepen the core's color density and edge contrast so the form stays solid and unmistakable. Avoid a pedestal, base, dish, or platform beneath the form, see-through transparency that dissolves the silhouette, environmental reflections, tiny details, complex internal structures, murkiness that reads as dirt, and plastic-looking material. The result should feel serene, premium, and quietly futuristic: one glowing sculptural symbol. No pseudo-text, labels, letters, or logos. Keep every critical part within the central 80 percent of the canvas. Use bold, simple forms without details that disappear at small display sizes.
